facts.statement: Fylax is a genus of hadrosauroid ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Spain.
facts.quote: Fylax (meaning "keeper") is a genus of hadrosauroid ornithopod from the Late Cretaceous Figuerola Formation of Spain.

facts.statement: The genus Fylax contains only one known species, Fylax thyrakolasus, which is known from a nearly complete left dentary bone.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Fylax thyrakolasus, known from a nearly complete left dentary.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Fylax, designated IPS-36338, was discovered in the early 1990s.
facts.quote: The holotype of Fylax, IPS-36338, a left dentary, was discovered in the early 1990s.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in the Figuerola Formation in Lleida province, northeastern Spain.
facts.quote: It was found in the Figuerola Formation in Lleida province, northeastern Spain.

facts.statement: The dentary was initially described as a distinct fossil in 1999.
The names Fylax and thyrakolasus combine to mean "keeper of the gates of hell," referencing the dinosaur's proximity to the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction event.
facts.quote: The generic name, Fylax, comes from the modern Greek, fýlax (keeper), and the specific name, thyrakolasus, comes from the Greek thýra (gate) and kólasi (hell), thus creating the combination "keeper of the gates of hell" in reference to the proximity of this taxon to the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction event.

facts.statement: Later phylogenetic analyses in 2026 failed to recover the close relationship between Fylax and Tethyshadros that was initially proposed in 2021.
facts.quote: In their 2026 description of Kryptohadros, Magyar and colleagues included Fylax in an updated version of the phylogenetic matrix of Longrich et al. (2024) and the similar but less extensive matrix of Dai et al. (2025). Both datasets failed to recover a close relationship between Fylax and Tethyshadros, as initially proposed in 2021.

facts.statement: Using updated matrices, some researchers placed Fylax as an early-diverging member of the Hadrosauridae rather than as a non-hadrosaurid hadrosauromorph.
facts.quote: Instead, Tethyhadros was recovered as the sister taxon of Kryptohadros in a clade also containing Telmatosaurus, deemed the Telmatosauridae. Using the latter matrix, Fylax was placed in a more derived position, as an early-diverging member of the Hadrosauridae.

facts.statement: Fylax lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 68 to 66 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 68 a 66 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Fylax lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
